1: Chapter 1: A Visitor in the Rain
It had been raining in Pierrefeu for three days. In the spring, Claire Martin’s older sister had left for Paris, and since then, Claire had been running the village’s small pharmacy alone.
When night fell, she closed the shutters, tallied the day’s takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone pounded on the door below. A man’s voice called out, “Is anyone there?”
On the doorstep stood a young man, soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a bloodstained cloth. He introduced himself as Pierre Lapin and said he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
“I need treatment,” Lapin said quietly. “I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred francs be enough?”
He pulled a letter from his jacket, wrapped in oilskin. “This letter must reach Saint-Vent Abbey before the eighteenth of May.”
Since her sister’s departure, Claire had often felt down in the evenings, but that night, she didn’t have time to dwell on it.
Still, she refused his money and said only, “At dawn tomorrow, I’ll take you into the mountains.”
2: At daybreak, they set off. Claire carried a basket on her back with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope, they came across old Gaston Roux splitting wood. He set down his axe and told them in a low voice that the night before, three strangers had questioned people at the village entrance about a wounded young man.
"Take the trail, little Claire," said Gaston Roux. "The main road isn't safe." Claire thanked him.
The trail was narrow and slippery. Claire walked ahead, placing each step with confidence. Lapin followed without a word.
By noon, the rain had stopped; the mist slowly lifted, and the roof of Saint-Vent Abbey appeared in the distance. Standing at the door was a nun, Sister Agnès, tasked with welcoming visitors.
Sister Agnès took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for two years."
Lapin said to Claire, "I owe you my life." Claire smiled. "Then next time, fix the roof of my pharmacy." Lapin stayed at the abbey.
That evening, Claire descended the mountain alone. When she reached home, night had already fallen; she lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
